newsitem.title: USA: Clinton thanks King Hussein, Mubarak on Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Clinton thanks King Hussein, Mubarak on Hebron.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Thursday thanked Jordan's King Hussein and Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak for their support for an agreement between Israel and the Palestinians on the West Bank city of Hebron.
National Security Adviser-designate Samuel Berger told network radio reporters that Clinton made morning phone calls to the two leaders thanking them for their roles.

Berger said the Hebron deal would not have been possible without the intervention of King Hussein and the support of Mubarak. The king kept talks between Israel and the Palestinians from collapsing last weekend with a compromise proposal.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat reached a deal on Tuesday on a partial Israeli troop withdrawal from Hebron.

White House spokesman Mike McCurry said Clinton stressed in the phone calls that all involved "need to emphasise to the parties that they should provide their maximum effort now to move forward, and that those who support the peace process should lend their maximum support to those who are making and implementing the peace."
Netanyahu, Arafat, King Hussein and Mubarak are all expected to visit the White House separately in the coming months, but Berger said no summit was planned.
"This is not a big summit. This will be a series of meetings," he said.
Berger said the meeting with Netanyahu would include discussions on "whether it is possible to resume negotiations with Syria toward a peace agreement."
"It has always been the Israeli view that we share that a comprehensive peace is the ultimate objective and you can't have a comprehensive peace until you have Syria as part of it," he said.
